Item count I can stand behind; the rupee value I cannot, and here is why.

How many items: 612. Of the 1,372 stock-managed items that still show on-hand quantity in Oil, 612 have had no outward movement of any kind between 01-Aug-2025 and 30-Jul-2026 — nothing sold on an A/R invoice, nothing shipped on a delivery note, nothing issued or consumed on a goods issue (I scanned 8,765 invoices, 582 delivery notes and 4,402 goods issues over those twelve months).

But read that 612 with one big caveat: 362 of them are in the FIXED ASSETS item group — capex (puff panels, machines, a car, a Mac mini, workstations) that has been set up as inventory items. Strip those out and the genuine trading/stores dead list is 250 items: 185 packaging materials, 30 finished goods, 13 consumables, 12 trading items, 8 raw materials, 2 semi-finished. If you also treat a warehouse-to-warehouse transfer as 'movement', the strict list falls from 612 to 438 (78 excluding the fixed-asset group).

What it is worth: I cannot give you a reliable figure. SAP is only exposing a cost for part of the stock through this interface. Finished goods (batch-valued, CostAccountingMethod bis_SNB) and raw material come back with zero cost — 244 finished-goods items and 50 raw-material items on hand all price out at ₹0, which is obviously not real for a company billing ~₹33 Cr a month. Only packaging, trading and the fixed-asset group carry a readable warehouse average cost. On that readable slice the numbers are: total on-hand value ₹20.03 Cr, of which dead ₹16.94 Cr (84.6%) — but ₹16.85 Cr of that is a single fixed-asset line (FA0000005 PUFF PANELS AND ACCESSORIES, 362.5 units, ₹16.55 Cr) plus the rest of the FIXED ASSETS group. Excluding fixed assets, the dead stock that has a readable cost is only ₹9,39,916 out of ₹3.18 Cr of readable inventory (3.0%).

So: 612 items (250 excluding fixed assets) is a solid answer; ₹16.94 Cr / 84.6% is NOT a true dead-stock value or a true share, because the denominator is missing all finished-goods and raw-material value. To get the real number someone needs to run the Inventory Audit / stock valuation report inside SAP, or query the OINM/batch valuation layers directly — the Service Layer doesn't expose them.
